newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl pays tribute to Marshall Plan in parliament.
newsitem.headline: Kohl pays tribute to Marshall Plan in parliament.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl paid an emotional tribute in parliament on Thursday to the United States for its Marshall Plan aid programme that spurred West Germany's economic recovery after World War Two.

In a speech marking the 50th anniversary of a speech by George Marshall, then U.S. Secretary of State, that launched the aid programme for Europe, Kohl said Marshall's address had been a ray of hope for Europe.

"We will never forget what the people of the United States did for us Germans," Kohl said. "There were so many Americans who with their CARE packages and donations helped Germans in their hour of greatest need."

Kohl had earlier formally thanked the United States in a speech in Washington on June 5 -- the actual anniversary of Marshall's speech that paved the way for billions of dollars for European reconstruction.
Kohl, who was 17 at the time, said even though a majority of today's Germans were not even born when Marshall delivered his address, the Marshall plan had an effect on all Germans.

"For us it was more than economic help," Kohl said. "It was above all a message of solidarity, a message that the United States would not abandon Europe. It was also a message to the Europeans to come together and help each other. For us Germans, it meant a new beginning."
The chancellor said it was a great deed that for the first time in history a victorious nation had extended a helping hand after a war to the defeated nation.
